description: Screenshot of a Twitter thread by @jonrobweb (JohnnyNashville), Dec 28 2019 - Jan 28 2020. The original tweet, tagged #QAnon #WWG1WGA #Durham #RedPill, embeds an image of an early Q post's list of rhetorical questions with red hand-drawn annotations: a circle around the misspelling 'suppose' and a large red 'D.'. In replies, the poster claims misspellings in Q posts and POTUS tweets 'assist in decodes' and that this Q post referenced Durham, with the missing D as confirmation.
text: JohnnyNashville @jonrobweb · Dec 28, 2019. From the very beginning. #QAnon #WWG1WGA #Durham #RedPill. Does POTUS have the goods on most bad actors? Was TRUMP asked to run for President? Why? By Who? Was HRC next in line? Was the election suppose to be rigged? Did good people prevent the rigging? Why did POTUS form a panel to investigate? Has POTUS *ever* made a statement that did not become prove as true/fact? What is POTUS in control of? What is the one organization left that isn't corrupt? Why does the military play such a vital role? Why is POTUS surrounded by highly respected generals? Who guards former Presidents? Why is that relevant? 2. 42. 178. Juliepiemonte @juliepiemonte · 51m. Niiccceee! 1. 2. 12. Tuna @ACWest11 · 18m. I don't get it, can u explain? 1. JohnnyNashville @jonrobweb. Replying to @ACWest11 @juliepiemonte and 21 others. Misspellings are important. In Q posts (unless later corrected) and POTUS tweets. They assist in decodes. The above Q post was referencing Durham. Boat as hint, missing D as confirmation. 1:01 PM · Jan 28, 2020 · Twitter for Android.
flags: The 'misspelling decode' and Durham-reference claims are the tweeter's unverified interpretation
Trump, Clinton and Durham appear only as references in text, not in a photo

description: 'Q proof' graphic (Qproof137) on a black background pairing Q drop #3389 of Jul 9 2019 — which asks about 'Durham & Rogers meeting(s)?' and Adm. Rogers's retirement and Trump Tower visit — with a Dec 20 2019 Intercept article by Matthew Cole reporting that former NSA director Michael Rogers is cooperating with John Durham's probe and has met Durham on multiple occasions. Matching lines are highlighted in blue; the layout presents the article as validating the earlier drop.
text: Q PROOF:. Q !!mG7VJxZNCI ID: 0517d5 No.6968462 3389. Jul 9 2019 12:54:43 (EST). AG & Rogers meeting? Durham & Rogers meeting(s)? Why did Rogers retire? Why did Rogers visit POTUS @ TT w/o authorization shortly after a SCIF was installed? Why did select former ABC directors call for the removal of Rogers? Why did POTUS move his transition command center (base of ops) from TT the VERY NEXT DAY? Q. The Intercept_. FORMER NSA DIRECTOR IS COOPERATING WITH PROBE OF TRUMP-RUSSIA INVESTIGATION. Matthew Cole. December 20 2019, 3:17 p.m. RETIRED ADM. MICHAEL ROGERS, former director of the National Security Agency, has been cooperating with the Justice Department's probe into the origins of the counterintelligence investigation of the Trump presidential campaign's alleged ties to Russia, according to four people familiar with Rogers's participation. Rogers has met the prosecutor leading the probe, Connecticut U.S. Attorney John Durham, on multiple occasions, according to two people familiar with Rogers's cooperation. While the substance of those meetings is not clear, Rogers has cooperated voluntarily, several people with knowledge of the matter said. PROOFS ARE IMPORTANT — Q
